{{Short description|Shinto priest training organization}} {{Infobox organization | image = 皇典講究所.jpg | caption = Office of Japanese Classics Research at the end of the [[Meiji era]] | predecessor = [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]] | successor = [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], [[Kokugakuin University]] }} [[File:皇典講究所_發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|This monument is located in front of the [[Tokyo]] Kusei Kaikan in [[Iidabashi]], [[Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]], Tokyo. Tokyo Kusei Kaikan was the former location of the Office of Japanese Classics Research.{{Cite web |title=國學院大學の歴史 |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/6c60e6a689ef9e9f97528ca2780a67b1-1.pdf |access-date=2021-02-26 |publisher=國學院大學}} ]] The {{Nihongo|'''Institute of Japanese Classics Research'''|皇典講究所|Kōten Kōkyūsho}} was a central government organization for the training of the [[Kannushi|Shinto priesthood]] in Japan.https://archive.today/20230315184013/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8964{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213-214}}{{Sfn|デジタル大辞泉|pp=}}{{cite web |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230315184309/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-date=2023-03-15 |url-status=live |title=Shrine priest training institutes |website=kokugakuin.ac.jp }} It was established by the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji Government]] in 1882 as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito]] was its first head. Under pressure from the [[Occupation of Japan|Occupation Policy]] by the postwar [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]], it was dissolved in 1946. The [[Association of Shinto Shrines]] was established and merged the [[National Association of Shinto Priests]], [[Jingūkyō|Jingu-kyo]], and [[Institute of Divinities]] into the same organization.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=252-253}} Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of [[Kokugakuin University]]) was then established as a stand-alone corporation.{{Cite web |title=History of Kokugakuin University |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/2fd56c1ae975ec79a9200c208303283b.pdf |access-date=May 3, 2020 |publisher=Kokugakuin University }} == Overview == [[File:Stamp_of_Kōten-kōkyūsho_5.2.jpg|thumb|Imprint of the Office of Japanese Classics Research]] [[File:皇典講究所椅子.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Chairs used in the Imperial Lecture Hall in {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|qq=}}]] [[File:Tokyo_kusei_kaikan.jpg|thumb|333x333px|Tokyo Ward Government Building at the former location of the Imperial Palace Kosho]] This school was opened as an institution to carry out the indoctrination of the Imperial Way to the masses as part of the religious policy of the [[Meiji (era)|Meiji era]], when [[State Shinto]] was established.{{Sfn|世界宗教用語大事典|2004|pp=}}{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} In 1890, the organization expanded the educational business and opened Kokugakuin.{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} After its establishment, as part of its business, it began publishing the Imperial Lectures from 1889 (1889) February.{{Cite web |last=[[丸善雄松堂]] |date= |title=皇典講究所講演 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/micro/kensaku/meiji-2.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=丸善雄松堂 |quote=}} In 1890 (Meiji 23), a compilation project of [[Koji Ruien]] was carried out. The [[Engishiki]] was also compiled, and in 1931 (Showa 6), a revised Engishiki was published to commemorate the 1,000th anniversary of the Engishiki compilation. The Ministry of Home Affairs was commissioned to train [[Shinkan (official)|priests]] and [[Kannushi|priesthood]]s, and the Imperial Institute and Kokugakuin University Press published many reference books for the priesthood qualification examination.{{Cite web |last=國學院大學 |date= |title=近代—祓の制度化と大祓詞・中臣祓研究 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/kaihatsu/oharai/theme_d.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=國學院大學伝統文化リサーチセンター資料館 |quote=}} With the establishment of the [[Kyodo Shoku]], the priesthood was abolished as a [[Kyodo Shoku|teaching ministry]], and the main duties of the priesthood were limited to rituals.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Shinto priests who wanted to preach doctrine were marginalised into [[Sect Shinto]].{{Cite journal |last=Susumu |first=Shimazono |last2=島茴進 |last3=Murphy |first3=Regan E. |date=2009 |title=State Shinto in the Lives of the People: The Establishment of Emperor Worship, Modern Nationalism, and Shrine Shinto in Late Meiji |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30233855 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=93–124 |issn=0304-1042}} The state continued to treat [[Shinto]] as a non-religious institution due to [[Secular Shrine Theory]], while the priesthood continued to perform official state rituals.{{Sfn|松本久史|2011|pp=78-79}} When the foundation eventually developed into an incorporated foundation and the appearance of Shinto as the state religion came to an end and management became difficult, it was jointly run by private organizations related to [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] with the cooperation of Shintoists, along with the {{Nihongo|Dainippon Jingikai|大日本神祇会}} and {{Nihongo|Jingū Hōsaikai|神宮奉斎会}}, until then.{{Cite web |last=[[神社新報]] |date=2010 |title=神社新報の歩み |url=http://www.jinja.co.jp/ayumi03.html |access-date=2016-04-22 |publisher=神社新報社 |page= |quote=}} == History == Around the 10th year of Meiji (1877), during the [[Bunmei-kaika]] era, the slump of the [[Taikyo Proclamation|Proclamation of the Great Doctrine]] and the subsequent controversy over the ritual gods led to a proposal from within the government to establish a school focusing on [[Kokugaku]] research, and the subsequent controversy over the establishment of a school for [[Kokugaku]] studies. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882) August 23, [[Emperor Meiji]] appointed [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], his most trusted advisor, as the president.{{Cite web |last=[[木野主計]] |date= |title=『明治期國學研究雜誌集成』解題・総目次 : マイクロフィルム版 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/ysd_a_gc1644_li_kokugakuzasshi.pdf |access-date=2016-03-23 |publisher=[[雄松堂書店]] |quote=}} In the same year, [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] and other [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] [[Bureaucrat|High official]], and several [[Japanese literature]] scholars, including [[Iidabashi|Iidacho]], on November 4 of the same year.{{Cite web |last=京都國學院 |date= |title=学院の沿革 |url=http://kyoto-kokugakuin.ac.jp/enkaku.html |access-date=2016-03-15 |publisher=学校法人京都皇典研究所 京都國學院 |quote=}} The Imperial Academy was established with two divisions: the Faculty of Letters, which consisted of the four departments of shumon, history, law, and writing, and the Faculty of Work, which consisted of the three departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics. According to the "Establishment Announcement" issued at the opening of the school, the philosophy and purpose of the Faculty of Literature was to "teach the national scriptures", "cultivate morality", "cultivate talent through Chinese and Western studies", "cultivate men of national utility", and "promote the beauty of the nation abroad.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} In 1888 (Meiji 21), six years after the opening of the school, the regulations were revised. According to the prospectus for the revision, the institute was to be an institution for the training of students specializing in Japanese literature, and it was to convene experts in Japanese literature to study every detail of Japanese literature that should be documented in the present day. The three departments were Political Science, Legislation, and Literature, with the Literature Department offering courses in language, writing, customs, natural products, crafts, fine arts, agriculture, and geography.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} Later, in 1890 (Meiji 23), the Kokugakuin, which taught national history, national literature, and national law, was opened at the Imperial Academy, and the place dedicated to national law was named the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} (which developed into [[Nihon University]]).{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} On January 25, 1946 (Showa 21), after the end of [[World War II]], the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]] dissolved the Imperial Academy and [[Kokugakuin University]] was established. The Nihon Law School initially held lectures at night in classrooms rented from the Imperial Law School. [[Nihon University]], because of its close relationship with the Imperial Academy, began offering Shinto courses in 1924 for the purpose of re-educating Shinto teachers, and the Shinto Scholarship Association was organized by the Shinto Sect United Association (later [[Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto Federation]]). The Shinto Scholarship Society was organized. === Chronology === ==== From inception to dissolution ==== * 1882 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]]15) - Established as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. The dual role of Shinto priests as instructors was abolished.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Gendo Yano is appointed as the first Dean of the Faculty of Letters, and [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]] is appointed as the first President. The school is located in [[Tokyo Prefecture]], Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku (now [[Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]][[Iidabashi]]), and the '''Imperial Academy''' is established. * 1884 (Meiji 17) - Movement to transfer the Imperial Academy to a government-run institution (-18th year of Meiji) aborted due to the death of Prince Noborito in 1904. * 1887 (Meiji 20) - The first graduation ceremony of the Imperial Academy. The alumni association "Suihokai" was established. (This is regarded as the founding of Kokugakuin Daigakuin Inyu-kai). * 1888 (Meiji 21) - [[Hibiya High School|Furitsu Ichi Junior High School]] principal Yoshito Maruyama, Isao Matsuno, Sunao Motoda, Sadasuke Imaizumi, and others establish a supplementary junior high school at the Imperial Academy. Later reorganized as Kyoritsu Junior High School, a private school. * 1889 (1889) - [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] becomes the first director of the Imperial Academy. The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} is established within the Imperial Academy. (''Predecessor of Nihon University Law School''). * 1890 (23rd year of Meiji) - Kokugakuin established as an educational institution within the Imperial Academy. * 1893 (1893) - The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} becomes a designated school of the Ministry of Justice, and its graduates are qualified to take the examination for appointment as judges and prosecutors. * 1894 (27th year of Meiji) - Kyoritsu Junior High School was renamed Johoku Junior High School and transferred to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. (The predecessor of ''[[Tokyo Metropolitan Toyama High School|Toyama High School]]'', Johoku Junior High School, Johoku High School, etc.) * 1895 (28th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} moved to Dainippon Kyoiku Kai (located in [[Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|Hitotsubashi]] Street, Kanda-ku). * 1896 (29th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} reorganized as an incorporated foundation and became organizationally independent from the Imperial Academy. * 1898 (31st year of Meiji) - The Imperial Academy is approved as an incorporated foundation. * 1899 (32nd year of Meiji) - [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] entrusted with the training of priests. * 1900 (33rd year of Meiji) - Establishment of the Reiten Investigation Committee. * 1909 (1909) - The Priesthood Training Department was established. * 1923 (1923) - Moved to the Imperial estate behind Shibuya Hikawa. * 1930 (1930|1930) - The shrine was reopened. * 1944 (Showa 19) - The Kokugaku Kenkyusho (Kokugaku Research Institute) was established. * 1946 (1946) - In response to pressure from the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|General Headquarters of the Allied Forces]] occupation, the institute was dissolved in January. The following month, the [[Religious corporation]] [[Association of Shinto Shrines|Shrine Headquarters]] was established. It was merged together with the Dai Nihon Kagimikai and the Jingu Bonsai Kai, and in March, Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of ''Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation'') was established as a stand-alone corporation. ==== After dissolution ==== * 1955 (1955) - The Institute of Japanese Studies at Kokugakuin University was established and took over the research of the Imperial Academy. * 1985 (1985) - [[Nihon University]] and Kokugakuin University jointly erected a monument at the site of the Imperial Academy (3-5-5 [[Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]in front of the Tokyo Kusei Kaikan). * 2007 (Heisei 19) - Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation registered the Imperial Academy as a trademark. Registration No. 5018534.{{Cite web |title=登録5018534 J-PlatPat/AIPN |url=https://www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp/t0201 |access-date=2020-05-05 |website=www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp |publisher=}} == Basic Data == * Location: 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, [[Tokyo City|Tokyo]] (current [[Tokyo]] [[Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]) * Area: 1,666 tsubo (1,666 m2), 1 kyu 9 shaku (1,666 tsubo, 1 kyu 9 shaku) * Capacity: 300 students === Course of study (at the time of establishment) === * Main course: 3 years, Preliminary course: 2 years ** Faculty of Literature (4 departments: Shushoku, History, Laws and Regulations, and Writing) ** Work Department: 2 departments (3 departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics) == Remarks == ; Notice On November 4, 1882, the school announced its intention to become a {{ill|Modern Japanese government system|lt=modern nation's|ja|近代日本の官制|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern Japanese government system|qq=}} academic school (Gakko, synonymous with "school" and read the same as "school").[http://www.dsecchi.mext.go.jp/d_1204t/pdf/kokugakuin_1204tsecchi_syushi1.pdf 設置の趣旨等を記載した書類 - 大学設置室 - 文部科学省] On November 4, 1882, the government announced its intention to establish a modern national school (gakko, which is synonymous with "school" and reads the same way) for the study of Japan's original studies.
{{Quote frame|The Imperial Household Law Institution is built. We have selected Yoshitatsu to conduct the opening ceremony of the school today. The General Judge Noboru Hitoshi, who has been entrusted with the responsibility of presiding over the ceremony, addresses the staff and students in a friendly manner. The path of learning is far greater than the path of books. The teaching of the national form will strengthen the foundation of our nation and cultivate our moral character. and cultivate moral values in order to aim for the true purpose of life. This is a rule that should not be forgotten by the next generation. This is why we must establish this school Now after the staff student, this is the body of the body Takamasa Honjou Eternal Second Period Seyo November 4, 1897 Prince Arisugawa Takahito}}
; Date of Establishment The establishment of the school was officially approved on August 23, 1882, and the opening ceremony was scheduled to take place on September 1, but was postponed due to the health condition of the president, Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa, and the school was opened on November 4. Classes were held from September. On June 3, the school site was set at the residence of former Hatamoto Hayato Akimoto, 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo, and on August 21, an "Application for the Establishment of an Imperial Institute for the Study of the Imperial Law" was sent in the name of Vice President of the Shinto School Hei Iwashitara [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], the Vice President of Shintoism, and was approved on the 23rd of the same month. The date of registration of the [[Foundation (nonprofit)]] was later changed to the date of its establishment.國學院大學（『百二十周年小史』参照） == Public and private schools == {{Multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | header_align = center | footer_align = left/right/center | image1 = Nihon University Place of opening.jpg | width1 = 150 | alt1 = | caption1 = Nihon University, the site of the school's founding. | image2 = Kokugakuin University Place of opening.jpg | width2 = 150 | alt2 = | caption2 = Kokugakuin University Opening Place }} The Imperial Academy established an institution for [[research]] on its premises. The director, Akiyoshi Yamada [[Minister of Justice (Japan)|Minister of Justice]], founded the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} in 1889 (Meiji 22), followed by the Kokugakuin in the following year. He subsequently fostered public and private law schools.{{Cite web |last=[[萩市観光協会]] |date= |title=初代司法大臣で日大・国学院の学祖 山田顕義誕生地 （顕義園） |url=http://www.hagishi.com/search/detail.php?d=1100163 |access-date=2016-05-12 |publisher=萩市観光協会「ぶらり萩あるき」 |page= |quote=}} Law School In 1889, the Minister of Justice, Yamada Kengi, who was the director of the Imperial Academy, established an educational institution within the Imperial Academy for the purpose of researching Japan's unique [[Code of law]] using ancient Japanese and foreign laws as a means of improving Japan's legal system. ; Kokugakuin Following the Law School, the Kokugakuin was established in 1890 to study national history, national literature, and [[Statute|national law]], and to promote [[Kokugaku|national studies]] and to train priests as an institution for teaching the concept of the nation, or national direction and Shinto.[http://www.kokugakuin.ac.jp/guide/shuisho.html 國學院設立趣意書] == Positions held == For [[Kokugakuin University]], see [[Kokugakuin University#People and organizations related to Kokugakuin]] === President === * [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], February 1882 - January 1886. * [[Prince Tsunehisa Takeda]], May 1908-. * [[Prince Naruhisa Kitashirakawa]] 1908-1924 * [[Prince Kuni Kuniyoshi|Kunihiko Kuniyoshi]], November 1927 - 1930 * Prince [[Prince Kan'in Kotohito|Prince Kaniinomiya]], 1930 - 1945 * [[Prince Nashimoto Morimasa|Prince Morimasa Nashimoto]] 1945-1946 === Vice President === * [[Kuga Tatemichi]], September 1882-] * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] April 1918-June 1921 * [[:en:Egi Kazuyuki|Egi Senyuki]] August 1932-. * [[Hiranuma Kiichirō]], 1945- === Director === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] January 1889 - 1895 * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] June 1896 - March 1910 * [[Yoshikawa Akimasa]] March 1910-March 1911 * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] March 1911-April 1918 * [[Hijikata Hisamoto|Hisamoto Hijikata]], 1919- * [[Eitaro Komatsubara]], 1919-1920 * [[Ichiki Kitokurō|Kitokurō Ichiki]] 1920-1925 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], February 1925-August 1932 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], 1933- * [[Yukitada Sasaki]] May 1936-March 1946 === Secretary General === * Shigetake Sugiura May 1899- * Shinichiro Yamada 1912 - 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- === Secretary === * Noboru Takayama 1902- * Momoki Kamo 1903 * Momoki Kamo April 1903-October 1905 * Iwakichi Ishikawa 1909- * Yoshiki Kuwahara 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- * Tomokazu Soejima 1926 (Taisho 15)- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1918- * Yoshiki Iwamoto 1924- * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- * Noboru Takayama 1937- * [[Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat)|Shigeru Yoshida]] === Board of directors === * Sadasuke Imaizumi Toyoji Wada 1921- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat) * Shozo Kono 1935- * Naoichiro Ueki 1945- == Others == As a reorganization of the former [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] due to the separation of teachings and studies, the Imperial Academy was decided upon by a motion made after the conclusion of the Grand Council on Shintoism by Home Minister Yamada Kenyoshi, who was appointed to the Shinto Interdisciplinary Office at the time.The Imperial Academy, which was based on the [[Shinto Office Student Dormitory]] and expanded, was established from Yamada's It was established from a motion of the [[Kensho]] In 1885 [[:en:Cabinet of Japan|Cabinet System]] was established, and in 1886 [[Itō Hirobumi]] established a government official training institute. 1889 [[Meiji Constitution|The Constitution of the Empire of Japan]] was enacted, which shifted the focus from imperial studies to government-oriented [[Higher education]] system. The priesthood training institutions were transformed into official training institutions under Ito's policy of establishing the Imperial University Ordinance. Thus, the establishment of [[:en:Benefit corporation|public interest corporation]] under Act No. 89 of [[:en:1896|1894]] came into effect, and the new [[Civil law (common law)|Civil law]] of 1898 transformed the organization into a foundation (public interest corporation), which was the modern organization at the time.In the same year, the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} also made the same transition. == Annotations == === Notes === {{Reflist|group="note"}} === References === {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * 『皇典講究所五十年史』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|1035528}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1932nd year * 『皇典講究所改正要領』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|815303}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1889th year 6月 * 『皇典講究所草創期の人々』、[[Kokugakuin University|國學院大學]]、本居豊穎、1982nd year 2月 * 『明治期國學研究雑誌集成』、國學院大學、木野主計、雄松堂出版、1996th year 11月 * {{Cite book |last=新田均・武田秀章 |title=わかりやすい神道の歴史 |publisher=神社新報社 |year=2005 |isbn=9784915265051 |editor-last=神社本庁研修所 |chapter=第六章 明治維新以後（近代）、現代 |ref={{Sfnref|Nitta|Takeda|2005}} |language=ja |trans-title=An Easy-to-Understand History of Shinto. }} * {{Cite book |last1=松本久史 |title=プレステップ神道学 {{Short description|Shinto priest training organization}} {{Infobox organization | image = 皇典講究所.jpg | caption = Office of Japanese Classics Research at the end of the [[Meiji era]] | predecessor = [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]] | successor = [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], [[Kokugakuin University]] }} [[File:皇典講究所_發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|This monument is located in front of the [[Tokyo]] Kusei Kaikan in [[Iidabashi]], [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]], Tokyo. Tokyo Kusei Kaikan was the former location of the Office of Japanese Classics Research.{{Cite web |title=國學院大學の歴史 |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/6c60e6a689ef9e9f97528ca2780a67b1-1.pdf |access-date=2021-02-26 |publisher=國學院大學}} ]] The {{Nihongo|'''Institute of Japanese Classics Research'''|皇典講究所|Kōten Kōkyūsho}} was a central government organization for the training of the [[Kannushi|Shinto priesthood]] in Japan.https://archive.today/20230315184013/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8964{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213-214}}{{Sfn|デジタル大辞泉|pp=}}{{cite web |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230315184309/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-date=2023-03-15 |url-status=live |title=Shrine priest training institutes |website=kokugakuin.ac.jp }} It was established by the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji Government]] in 1882 as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito]] was its first head. Under pressure from the [[Occupation of Japan|Occupation Policy]] by the postwar [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]], it was dissolved in 1946. The [[Association of Shinto Shrines]] was established and merged the [[National Association of Shinto Priests]], [[Jingūkyō|Jingu-kyo]], and [[Institute of Divinities]] into the same organization.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=252-253}} Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of [[Kokugakuin University]]) was then established as a stand-alone corporation.{{Cite web |title=History of Kokugakuin University |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/2fd56c1ae975ec79a9200c208303283b.pdf |access-date=May 3, 2020 |publisher=Kokugakuin University }} == Overview == [[File:Stamp_of_Kōten-kōkyūsho_5.2.jpg|thumb|Imprint of the Office of Japanese Classics Research]] [[File:皇典講究所椅子.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Chairs used in the Imperial Lecture Hall in {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|qq=}}]] [[File:Tokyo_kusei_kaikan.jpg|thumb|333x333px|Tokyo Ward Government Building at the former location of the Imperial Palace Kosho]] This school was opened as an institution to carry out the indoctrination of the Imperial Way to the masses as part of the religious policy of the [[Meiji (era)|Meiji era]], when [[State Shinto]] was established.{{Sfn|世界宗教用語大事典|2004|pp=}}{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} In 1890, the organization expanded the educational business and opened Kokugakuin.{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} After its establishment, as part of its business, it began publishing the Imperial Lectures from 1889 (1889) February.{{Cite web |last=[[丸善雄松堂]] |date= |title=皇典講究所講演 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/micro/kensaku/meiji-2.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=丸善雄松堂 |quote=}} In 1890 (Meiji 23), a compilation project of [[Koji Ruien]] was carried out. The [[Engishiki]] was also compiled, and in 1931 (Showa 6), a revised Engishiki was published to commemorate the 1,000th anniversary of the Engishiki compilation. The Ministry of Home Affairs was commissioned to train [[Shinkan (official)|priests]] and [[Kannushi|priesthood]]s, and the Imperial Institute and Kokugakuin University Press published many reference books for the priesthood qualification examination.{{Cite web |last=國學院大學 |date= |title=近代—祓の制度化と大祓詞・中臣祓研究 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/kaihatsu/oharai/theme_d.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=國學院大學伝統文化リサーチセンター資料館 |quote=}} With the establishment of the [[Kyodo Shoku]], the priesthood was abolished as a [[Kyodo Shoku|teaching ministry]], and the main duties of the priesthood were limited to rituals.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Shinto priests who wanted to preach doctrine were marginalised into [[Sect Shinto]].{{Cite journal |last=Susumu |first=Shimazono |last2=島茴進 |last3=Murphy |first3=Regan E. |date=2009 |title=State Shinto in the Lives of the People: The Establishment of Emperor Worship, Modern Nationalism, and Shrine Shinto in Late Meiji |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30233855 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=93–124 |issn=0304-1042}} The state continued to treat [[Shinto]] as a non-religious institution due to [[Secular Shrine Theory]], while the priesthood continued to perform official state rituals.{{Sfn|松本久史|2011|pp=78-79}} When the foundation eventually developed into an incorporated foundation and the appearance of Shinto as the state religion came to an end and management became difficult, it was jointly run by private organizations related to [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] with the cooperation of Shintoists, along with the {{Nihongo|Dainippon Jingikai|大日本神祇会}} and {{Nihongo|Jingū Hōsaikai|神宮奉斎会}}, until then.{{Cite web |last=[[神社新報]] |date=2010 |title=神社新報の歩み |url=http://www.jinja.co.jp/ayumi03.html |access-date=2016-04-22 |publisher=神社新報社 |page= |quote=}} == History == Around the 10th year of Meiji (1877), during the [[Bunmei-kaika]] era, the slump of the [[Taikyo Proclamation|Proclamation of the Great Doctrine]] and the subsequent controversy over the ritual gods led to a proposal from within the government to establish a school focusing on [[Kokugaku]] research, and the subsequent controversy over the establishment of a school for [[Kokugaku]] studies. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882) August 23, [[Emperor Meiji]] appointed [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], his most trusted advisor, as the president.{{Cite web |last=[[木野主計]] |date= |title=『明治期國學研究雜誌集成』解題・総目次 : マイクロフィルム版 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/ysd_a_gc1644_li_kokugakuzasshi.pdf |access-date=2016-03-23 |publisher=[[雄松堂書店]] |quote=}} In the same year, [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] and other [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] [[Bureaucrat|High official]], and several [[Japanese literature]] scholars, including [[Iidabashi|Iidacho]], on November 4 of the same year.{{Cite web |last=京都國學院 |date= |title=学院の沿革 |url=http://kyoto-kokugakuin.ac.jp/enkaku.html |access-date=2016-03-15 |publisher=学校法人京都皇典研究所 京都國學院 |quote=}} The Imperial Academy was established with two divisions: the Faculty of Letters, which consisted of the four departments of shumon, history, law, and writing, and the Faculty of Work, which consisted of the three departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics. According to the "Establishment Announcement" issued at the opening of the school, the philosophy and purpose of the Faculty of Literature was to "teach the national scriptures", "cultivate morality", "cultivate talent through Chinese and Western studies", "cultivate men of national utility", and "promote the beauty of the nation abroad.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} In 1888 (Meiji 21), six years after the opening of the school, the regulations were revised. According to the prospectus for the revision, the institute was to be an institution for the training of students specializing in Japanese literature, and it was to convene experts in Japanese literature to study every detail of Japanese literature that should be documented in the present day. The three departments were Political Science, Legislation, and Literature, with the Literature Department offering courses in language, writing, customs, natural products, crafts, fine arts, agriculture, and geography.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} Later, in 1890 (Meiji 23), the Kokugakuin, which taught national history, national literature, and national law, was opened at the Imperial Academy, and the place dedicated to national law was named the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} (which developed into [[Nihon University]]).{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} On January 25, 1946 (Showa 21), after the end of [[World War II]], the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]] dissolved the Imperial Academy and [[Kokugakuin University]] was established. The Nihon Law School initially held lectures at night in classrooms rented from the Imperial Law School. [[Nihon University]], because of its close relationship with the Imperial Academy, began offering Shinto courses in 1924 for the purpose of re-educating Shinto teachers, and the Shinto Scholarship Association was organized by the Shinto Sect United Association (later [[Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto Federation]]). The Shinto Scholarship Society was organized. === Chronology === ==== From inception to dissolution ==== * 1882 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]]15) - Established as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. The dual role of Shinto priests as instructors was abolished.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Gendo Yano is appointed as the first Dean of the Faculty of Letters, and [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]] is appointed as the first President. The school is located in [[Tokyo Prefecture]], Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku (now [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]][[Iidabashi]]), and the '''Imperial Academy''' is established. * 1884 (Meiji 17) - Movement to transfer the Imperial Academy to a government-run institution (-18th year of Meiji) aborted due to the death of Prince Noborito in 1904. * 1887 (Meiji 20) - The first graduation ceremony of the Imperial Academy. The alumni association "Suihokai" was established. (This is regarded as the founding of Kokugakuin Daigakuin Inyu-kai). * 1888 (Meiji 21) - [[Hibiya High School|Furitsu Ichi Junior High School]] principal Yoshito Maruyama, Isao Matsuno, Sunao Motoda, Sadasuke Imaizumi, and others establish a supplementary junior high school at the Imperial Academy. Later reorganized as Kyoritsu Junior High School, a private school. * 1889 (1889) - [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] becomes the first director of the Imperial Academy. The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} is established within the Imperial Academy. (''Predecessor of Nihon University Law School''). * 1890 (23rd year of Meiji) - Kokugakuin established as an educational institution within the Imperial Academy. * 1893 (1893) - The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} becomes a designated school of the Ministry of Justice, and its graduates are qualified to take the examination for appointment as judges and prosecutors. * 1894 (27th year of Meiji) - Kyoritsu Junior High School was renamed Johoku Junior High School and transferred to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. (The predecessor of ''[[Tokyo Metropolitan Toyama High School|Toyama High School]]'', Johoku Junior High School, Johoku High School, etc.) * 1895 (28th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} moved to Dainippon Kyoiku Kai (located in [[Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|Hitotsubashi]] Street, Kanda-ku). * 1896 (29th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} reorganized as an incorporated foundation and became organizationally independent from the Imperial Academy. * 1898 (31st year of Meiji) - The Imperial Academy is approved as an incorporated foundation. * 1899 (32nd year of Meiji) - [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] entrusted with the training of priests. * 1900 (33rd year of Meiji) - Establishment of the Reiten Investigation Committee. * 1909 (1909) - The Priesthood Training Department was established. * 1923 (1923) - Moved to the Imperial estate behind Shibuya Hikawa. * 1930 (1930|1930) - The shrine was reopened. * 1944 (Showa 19) - The Kokugaku Kenkyusho (Kokugaku Research Institute) was established. * 1946 (1946) - In response to pressure from the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|General Headquarters of the Allied Forces]] occupation, the institute was dissolved in January. The following month, the [[Religious corporation]] [[Association of Shinto Shrines|Shrine Headquarters]] was established. It was merged together with the Dai Nihon Kagimikai and the Jingu Bonsai Kai, and in March, Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of ''Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation'') was established as a stand-alone corporation. ==== After dissolution ==== * 1955 (1955) - The Institute of Japanese Studies at Kokugakuin University was established and took over the research of the Imperial Academy. * 1985 (1985) - [[Nihon University]] and Kokugakuin University jointly erected a monument at the site of the Imperial Academy (3-5-5 [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]in front of the Tokyo Kusei Kaikan). * 2007 (Heisei 19) - Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation registered the Imperial Academy as a trademark. Registration No. 5018534.{{Cite web |title=登録5018534 J-PlatPat/AIPN |url=https://www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp/t0201 |access-date=2020-05-05 |website=www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp |publisher=}} == Basic Data == * Location: 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, [[Tokyo City|Tokyo]] (current [[Tokyo]] [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]) * Area: 1,666 tsubo (1,666 m2), 1 kyu 9 shaku (1,666 tsubo, 1 kyu 9 shaku) * Capacity: 300 students === Course of study (at the time of establishment) === * Main course: 3 years, Preliminary course: 2 years ** Faculty of Literature (4 departments: Shushoku, History, Laws and Regulations, and Writing) ** Work Department: 2 departments (3 departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics) == Remarks == ; Notice On November 4, 1882, the school announced its intention to become a {{ill|Modern Japanese government system|lt=modern nation's|ja|近代日本の官制|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern Japanese government system|qq=}} academic school (Gakko, synonymous with "school" and read the same as "school").[http://www.dsecchi.mext.go.jp/d_1204t/pdf/kokugakuin_1204tsecchi_syushi1.pdf 設置の趣旨等を記載した書類 - 大学設置室 - 文部科学省] On November 4, 1882, the government announced its intention to establish a modern national school (gakko, which is synonymous with "school" and reads the same way) for the study of Japan's original studies.
{{Quote frame|The Imperial Household Law Institution is built. We have selected Yoshitatsu to conduct the opening ceremony of the school today. The General Judge Noboru Hitoshi, who has been entrusted with the responsibility of presiding over the ceremony, addresses the staff and students in a friendly manner. The path of learning is far greater than the path of books. The teaching of the national form will strengthen the foundation of our nation and cultivate our moral character. and cultivate moral values in order to aim for the true purpose of life. This is a rule that should not be forgotten by the next generation. This is why we must establish this school Now after the staff student, this is the body of the body Takamasa Honjou Eternal Second Period Seyo November 4, 1897 Prince Arisugawa Takahito}}
; Date of Establishment The establishment of the school was officially approved on August 23, 1882, and the opening ceremony was scheduled to take place on September 1, but was postponed due to the health condition of the president, Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa, and the school was opened on November 4. Classes were held from September. On June 3, the school site was set at the residence of former Hatamoto Hayato Akimoto, 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo, and on August 21, an "Application for the Establishment of an Imperial Institute for the Study of the Imperial Law" was sent in the name of Vice President of the Shinto School Hei Iwashitara [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], the Vice President of Shintoism, and was approved on the 23rd of the same month. The date of registration of the [[Foundation (nonprofit)]] was later changed to the date of its establishment.國學院大學（『百二十周年小史』参照） == Public and private schools == {{Multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | header_align = center | footer_align = left/right/center | image1 = Nihon University Place of opening.jpg | width1 = 150 | alt1 = | caption1 = Nihon University, the site of the school's founding. | image2 = Kokugakuin University Place of opening.jpg | width2 = 150 | alt2 = | caption2 = Kokugakuin University Opening Place }} The Imperial Academy established an institution for [[research]] on its premises. The director, Akiyoshi Yamada [[Minister of Justice (Japan)|Minister of Justice]], founded the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} in 1889 (Meiji 22), followed by the Kokugakuin in the following year. He subsequently fostered public and private law schools.{{Cite web |last=[[萩市観光協会]] |date= |title=初代司法大臣で日大・国学院の学祖 山田顕義誕生地 （顕義園） |url=http://www.hagishi.com/search/detail.php?d=1100163 |access-date=2016-05-12 |publisher=萩市観光協会「ぶらり萩あるき」 |page= |quote=}} Law School In 1889, the Minister of Justice, Yamada Kengi, who was the director of the Imperial Academy, established an educational institution within the Imperial Academy for the purpose of researching Japan's unique [[Code of law]] using ancient Japanese and foreign laws as a means of improving Japan's legal system. ; Kokugakuin Following the Law School, the Kokugakuin was established in 1890 to study national history, national literature, and [[Statute|national law]], and to promote [[Kokugaku|national studies]] and to train priests as an institution for teaching the concept of the nation, or national direction and Shinto.[http://www.kokugakuin.ac.jp/guide/shuisho.html 國學院設立趣意書] == Positions held == For [[Kokugakuin University]], see [[Kokugakuin University#People and organizations related to Kokugakuin]] === President === * [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], February 1882 - January 1886. * [[Prince Tsunehisa Takeda]], May 1908-. * [[Prince Naruhisa Kitashirakawa]] 1908-1924 * [[Prince Kuni Kuniyoshi|Kunihiko Kuniyoshi]], November 1927 - 1930 * Prince [[Prince Kan'in Kotohito|Prince Kaniinomiya]], 1930 - 1945 * [[Prince Nashimoto Morimasa|Prince Morimasa Nashimoto]] 1945-1946 === Vice President === * [[Kuga Tatemichi]], September 1882-] * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] April 1918-June 1921 * [[:en:Egi Kazuyuki|Egi Senyuki]] August 1932-. * [[Hiranuma Kiichirō]], 1945- === Director === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] January 1889 - 1895 * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] June 1896 - March 1910 * [[Yoshikawa Akimasa]] March 1910-March 1911 * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] March 1911-April 1918 * [[Hijikata Hisamoto|Hisamoto Hijikata]], 1919- * [[Eitaro Komatsubara]], 1919-1920 * [[Ichiki Kitokurō|Kitokurō Ichiki]] 1920-1925 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], February 1925-August 1932 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], 1933- * [[Yukitada Sasaki]] May 1936-March 1946 === Secretary General === * Shigetake Sugiura May 1899- * Shinichiro Yamada 1912 - 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- === Secretary === * Noboru Takayama 1902- * Momoki Kamo 1903 * Momoki Kamo April 1903-October 1905 * Iwakichi Ishikawa 1909- * Yoshiki Kuwahara 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- * Tomokazu Soejima 1926 (Taisho 15)- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1918- * Yoshiki Iwamoto 1924- * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- * Noboru Takayama 1937- * [[Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat)|Shigeru Yoshida]] === Board of directors === * Sadasuke Imaizumi Toyoji Wada 1921- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat) * Shozo Kono 1935- * Naoichiro Ueki 1945- == Others == As a reorganization of the former [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] due to the separation of teachings and studies, the Imperial Academy was decided upon by a motion made after the conclusion of the Grand Council on Shintoism by Home Minister Yamada Kenyoshi, who was appointed to the Shinto Interdisciplinary Office at the time.The Imperial Academy, which was based on the [[Shinto Office Student Dormitory]] and expanded, was established from Yamada's It was established from a motion of the [[Kensho]] In 1885 [[:en:Cabinet of Japan|Cabinet System]] was established, and in 1886 [[Itō Hirobumi]] established a government official training institute. 1889 [[Meiji Constitution|The Constitution of the Empire of Japan]] was enacted, which shifted the focus from imperial studies to government-oriented [[Higher education]] system. The priesthood training institutions were transformed into official training institutions under Ito's policy of establishing the Imperial University Ordinance. Thus, the establishment of [[:en:Benefit corporation|public interest corporation]] under Act No. 89 of [[:en:1896|1894]] came into effect, and the new [[Civil law (common law)|Civil law]] of 1898 transformed the organization into a foundation (public interest corporation), which was the modern organization at the time.In the same year, the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} also made the same transition. == Annotations == === Notes === {{Reflist|group="note"}} === References === {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * 『皇典講究所五十年史』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|1035528}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1932nd year * 『皇典講究所改正要領』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|815303}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1889th year 6月 * 『皇典講究所草創期の人々』、[[Kokugakuin University|國學院大學]]、本居豊穎、1982nd year 2月 * 『明治期國學研究雑誌集成』、國學院大學、木野主計、雄松堂出版、1996th year 11月 * {{Cite book |last=新田均・武田秀章 |title=わかりやすい神道の歴史 |publisher=神社新報社 |year=2005 |isbn=9784915265051 |editor-last=神社本庁研修所 |chapter=第六章 明治維新以後（近代）、現代 |ref={{Sfnref|Nitta|Takeda|2005}} |language=ja |trans-title=An Easy-to-Understand History of Shinto. }} * {{Cite book |last1=松本久史 |title=プレステップ神道学 {{Short description|Shinto priest training organization}} {{Infobox organization | image = 皇典講究所.jpg | caption = Office of Japanese Classics Research at the end of the [[Meiji era]] | predecessor = [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]] | successor = [[Association of Shinto Shrines]], [[Kokugakuin University]] }} [[File:皇典講究所_發祥記念碑.jpg|thumb|This monument is located in front of the [[Tokyo]] Kusei Kaikan in [[Iidabashi]], [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]], Tokyo. Tokyo Kusei Kaikan was the former location of the Office of Japanese Classics Research.{{Cite web |title=國學院大學の歴史 |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/6c60e6a689ef9e9f97528ca2780a67b1-1.pdf |access-date=2021-02-26 |publisher=國學院大學}} ]] The {{Nihongo|'''Institute of Japanese Classics Research'''|皇典講究所|Kōten Kōkyūsho}} was a central government organization for the training of the [[Kannushi|Shinto priesthood]] in Japan.https://archive.today/20230315184013/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8964{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213-214}}{{Sfn|デジタル大辞泉|pp=}}{{cite web |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230315184309/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8854 |archive-date=2023-03-15 |url-status=live |title=Shrine priest training institutes |website=kokugakuin.ac.jp }} It was established by the [[Meiji Restoration|Meiji Government]] in 1882 as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito]] was its first head. Under pressure from the [[Occupation of Japan|Occupation Policy]] by the postwar [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]], it was dissolved in 1946. The [[Association of Shinto Shrines]] was established and merged the [[National Association of Shinto Priests]], [[Jingūkyō|Jingu-kyo]], and [[Institute of Divinities]] into the same organization.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=252-253}} Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of [[Kokugakuin University]]) was then established as a stand-alone corporation.{{Cite web |title=History of Kokugakuin University |url=http://img.kokugakuin.ac.jp/assets/uploads/2017/06/2fd56c1ae975ec79a9200c208303283b.pdf |access-date=May 3, 2020 |publisher=Kokugakuin University }} == Overview == [[File:Stamp_of_Kōten-kōkyūsho_5.2.jpg|thumb|Imprint of the Office of Japanese Classics Research]] [[File:皇典講究所椅子.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Chairs used in the Imperial Lecture Hall in {{ill|Kokugakuin University Museum|ja|國學院大學博物館|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokugakuin University Museum|qq=}}]] [[File:Tokyo_kusei_kaikan.jpg|thumb|333x333px|Tokyo Ward Government Building at the former location of the Imperial Palace Kosho]] This school was opened as an institution to carry out the indoctrination of the Imperial Way to the masses as part of the religious policy of the [[Meiji (era)|Meiji era]], when [[State Shinto]] was established.{{Sfn|世界宗教用語大事典|2004|pp=}}{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} In 1890, the organization expanded the educational business and opened Kokugakuin.{{Sfn|ブリタニカ国際大百科事典 小項目事典|2014|pp=}} After its establishment, as part of its business, it began publishing the Imperial Lectures from 1889 (1889) February.{{Cite web |last=[[丸善雄松堂]] |date= |title=皇典講究所講演 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/micro/kensaku/meiji-2.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=丸善雄松堂 |quote=}} In 1890 (Meiji 23), a compilation project of [[Koji Ruien]] was carried out. The [[Engishiki]] was also compiled, and in 1931 (Showa 6), a revised Engishiki was published to commemorate the 1,000th anniversary of the Engishiki compilation. The Ministry of Home Affairs was commissioned to train [[Shinkan (official)|priests]] and [[Kannushi|priesthood]]s, and the Imperial Institute and Kokugakuin University Press published many reference books for the priesthood qualification examination.{{Cite web |last=國學院大學 |date= |title=近代—祓の制度化と大祓詞・中臣祓研究 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/kaihatsu/oharai/theme_d.html |access-date=2016-02-20 |publisher=國學院大學伝統文化リサーチセンター資料館 |quote=}} With the establishment of the [[Kyodo Shoku]], the priesthood was abolished as a [[Kyodo Shoku|teaching ministry]], and the main duties of the priesthood were limited to rituals.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Shinto priests who wanted to preach doctrine were marginalised into [[Sect Shinto]].{{Cite journal |last=Susumu |first=Shimazono |last2=島茴進 |last3=Murphy |first3=Regan E. |date=2009 |title=State Shinto in the Lives of the People: The Establishment of Emperor Worship, Modern Nationalism, and Shrine Shinto in Late Meiji |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/30233855 |journal=Japanese Journal of Religious Studies |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=93–124 |issn=0304-1042}} The state continued to treat [[Shinto]] as a non-religious institution due to [[Secular Shrine Theory]], while the priesthood continued to perform official state rituals.{{Sfn|松本久史|2011|pp=78-79}} When the foundation eventually developed into an incorporated foundation and the appearance of Shinto as the state religion came to an end and management became difficult, it was jointly run by private organizations related to [[Shinto shrine|shrine]] with the cooperation of Shintoists, along with the {{Nihongo|Dainippon Jingikai|大日本神祇会}} and {{Nihongo|Jingū Hōsaikai|神宮奉斎会}}, until then.{{Cite web |last=[[神社新報]] |date=2010 |title=神社新報の歩み |url=http://www.jinja.co.jp/ayumi03.html |access-date=2016-04-22 |publisher=神社新報社 |page= |quote=}} == History == Around the 10th year of Meiji (1877), during the [[Bunmei-kaika]] era, the slump of the [[Taikyo Proclamation|Proclamation of the Great Doctrine]] and the subsequent controversy over the ritual gods led to a proposal from within the government to establish a school focusing on [[Kokugaku]] research, and the subsequent controversy over the establishment of a school for [[Kokugaku]] studies. In the 15th year of Meiji (1882) August 23, [[Emperor Meiji]] appointed [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], his most trusted advisor, as the president.{{Cite web |last=[[木野主計]] |date= |title=『明治期國學研究雜誌集成』解題・総目次 : マイクロフィルム版 |url=http://myrp.maruzen.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/ysd_a_gc1644_li_kokugakuzasshi.pdf |access-date=2016-03-23 |publisher=[[雄松堂書店]] |quote=}} In the same year, [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] and other [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] [[Bureaucrat|High official]], and several [[Japanese literature]] scholars, including [[Iidabashi|Iidacho]], on November 4 of the same year.{{Cite web |last=京都國學院 |date= |title=学院の沿革 |url=http://kyoto-kokugakuin.ac.jp/enkaku.html |access-date=2016-03-15 |publisher=学校法人京都皇典研究所 京都國學院 |quote=}} The Imperial Academy was established with two divisions: the Faculty of Letters, which consisted of the four departments of shumon, history, law, and writing, and the Faculty of Work, which consisted of the three departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics. According to the "Establishment Announcement" issued at the opening of the school, the philosophy and purpose of the Faculty of Literature was to "teach the national scriptures", "cultivate morality", "cultivate talent through Chinese and Western studies", "cultivate men of national utility", and "promote the beauty of the nation abroad.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} In 1888 (Meiji 21), six years after the opening of the school, the regulations were revised. According to the prospectus for the revision, the institute was to be an institution for the training of students specializing in Japanese literature, and it was to convene experts in Japanese literature to study every detail of Japanese literature that should be documented in the present day. The three departments were Political Science, Legislation, and Literature, with the Literature Department offering courses in language, writing, customs, natural products, crafts, fine arts, agriculture, and geography.{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} Later, in 1890 (Meiji 23), the Kokugakuin, which taught national history, national literature, and national law, was opened at the Imperial Academy, and the place dedicated to national law was named the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} (which developed into [[Nihon University]]).{{Cite web |title=学部・学科等の理念・目的 |url=http://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/tenken/1-2rinen_gakubu(6-19).pdf |access-date=2020-08-20 |publisher=國學院大學}} On January 25, 1946 (Showa 21), after the end of [[World War II]], the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|GHQ]] dissolved the Imperial Academy and [[Kokugakuin University]] was established. The Nihon Law School initially held lectures at night in classrooms rented from the Imperial Law School. [[Nihon University]], because of its close relationship with the Imperial Academy, began offering Shinto courses in 1924 for the purpose of re-educating Shinto teachers, and the Shinto Scholarship Association was organized by the Shinto Sect United Association (later [[Sect Shinto|Sect Shinto Federation]]). The Shinto Scholarship Society was organized. === Chronology === ==== From inception to dissolution ==== * 1882 ([[Meiji (era)|Meiji]]15) - Established as the successor organization to the [[Bureau of Shinto Affairs]]. The dual role of Shinto priests as instructors was abolished.{{Sfn|Nitta|Takeda|2005|pp=213}} Gendo Yano is appointed as the first Dean of the Faculty of Letters, and [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]] is appointed as the first President. The school is located in [[Tokyo Prefecture]], Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku (now [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]][[Iidabashi]]), and the '''Imperial Academy''' is established. * 1884 (Meiji 17) - Movement to transfer the Imperial Academy to a government-run institution (-18th year of Meiji) aborted due to the death of Prince Noborito in 1904. * 1887 (Meiji 20) - The first graduation ceremony of the Imperial Academy. The alumni association "Suihokai" was established. (This is regarded as the founding of Kokugakuin Daigakuin Inyu-kai). * 1888 (Meiji 21) - [[Hibiya High School|Furitsu Ichi Junior High School]] principal Yoshito Maruyama, Isao Matsuno, Sunao Motoda, Sadasuke Imaizumi, and others establish a supplementary junior high school at the Imperial Academy. Later reorganized as Kyoritsu Junior High School, a private school. * 1889 (1889) - [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] becomes the first director of the Imperial Academy. The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} is established within the Imperial Academy. (''Predecessor of Nihon University Law School''). * 1890 (23rd year of Meiji) - Kokugakuin established as an educational institution within the Imperial Academy. * 1893 (1893) - The {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} becomes a designated school of the Ministry of Justice, and its graduates are qualified to take the examination for appointment as judges and prosecutors. * 1894 (27th year of Meiji) - Kyoritsu Junior High School was renamed Johoku Junior High School and transferred to [[Tokyo Prefecture]]. (The predecessor of ''[[Tokyo Metropolitan Toyama High School|Toyama High School]]'', Johoku Junior High School, Johoku High School, etc.) * 1895 (28th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} moved to Dainippon Kyoiku Kai (located in [[Hitotsubashi, Chiyoda|Hitotsubashi]] Street, Kanda-ku). * 1896 (29th year of Meiji) - {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} reorganized as an incorporated foundation and became organizationally independent from the Imperial Academy. * 1898 (31st year of Meiji) - The Imperial Academy is approved as an incorporated foundation. * 1899 (32nd year of Meiji) - [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] entrusted with the training of priests. * 1900 (33rd year of Meiji) - Establishment of the Reiten Investigation Committee. * 1909 (1909) - The Priesthood Training Department was established. * 1923 (1923) - Moved to the Imperial estate behind Shibuya Hikawa. * 1930 (1930|1930) - The shrine was reopened. * 1944 (Showa 19) - The Kokugaku Kenkyusho (Kokugaku Research Institute) was established. * 1946 (1946) - In response to pressure from the [[Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers|General Headquarters of the Allied Forces]] occupation, the institute was dissolved in January. The following month, the [[Religious corporation]] [[Association of Shinto Shrines|Shrine Headquarters]] was established. It was merged together with the Dai Nihon Kagimikai and the Jingu Bonsai Kai, and in March, Kokugakuin University Foundation (the predecessor of ''Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation'') was established as a stand-alone corporation. ==== After dissolution ==== * 1955 (1955) - The Institute of Japanese Studies at Kokugakuin University was established and took over the research of the Imperial Academy. * 1985 (1985) - [[Nihon University]] and Kokugakuin University jointly erected a monument at the site of the Imperial Academy (3-5-5 [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]in front of the Tokyo Kusei Kaikan). * 2007 (Heisei 19) - Kokugakuin University Educational Corporation registered the Imperial Academy as a trademark. Registration No. 5018534.{{Cite web |title=登録5018534 J-PlatPat/AIPN |url=https://www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp/t0201 |access-date=2020-05-05 |website=www.j-platpat.inpit.go.jp |publisher=}} == Basic Data == * Location: 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, [[Tokyo City|Tokyo]] (current [[Tokyo]] [[:en:Chiyoda, Tokyo|Chiyoda-ku]] [[Iidabashi]]) * Area: 1,666 tsubo (1,666 m2), 1 kyu 9 shaku (1,666 tsubo, 1 kyu 9 shaku) * Capacity: 300 students === Course of study (at the time of establishment) === * Main course: 3 years, Preliminary course: 2 years ** Faculty of Literature (4 departments: Shushoku, History, Laws and Regulations, and Writing) ** Work Department: 2 departments (3 departments of etiquette, music, and gymnastics) == Remarks == ; Notice On November 4, 1882, the school announced its intention to become a {{ill|Modern Japanese government system|lt=modern nation's|ja|近代日本の官制|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Modern Japanese government system|qq=}} academic school (Gakko, synonymous with "school" and read the same as "school").[http://www.dsecchi.mext.go.jp/d_1204t/pdf/kokugakuin_1204tsecchi_syushi1.pdf 設置の趣旨等を記載した書類 - 大学設置室 - 文部科学省] On November 4, 1882, the government announced its intention to establish a modern national school (gakko, which is synonymous with "school" and reads the same way) for the study of Japan's original studies.
{{Quote frame|The Imperial Household Law Institution is built. We have selected Yoshitatsu to conduct the opening ceremony of the school today. The General Judge Noboru Hitoshi, who has been entrusted with the responsibility of presiding over the ceremony, addresses the staff and students in a friendly manner. The path of learning is far greater than the path of books. The teaching of the national form will strengthen the foundation of our nation and cultivate our moral character. and cultivate moral values in order to aim for the true purpose of life. This is a rule that should not be forgotten by the next generation. This is why we must establish this school Now after the staff student, this is the body of the body Takamasa Honjou Eternal Second Period Seyo November 4, 1897 Prince Arisugawa Takahito}}
; Date of Establishment The establishment of the school was officially approved on August 23, 1882, and the opening ceremony was scheduled to take place on September 1, but was postponed due to the health condition of the president, Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa, and the school was opened on November 4. Classes were held from September. On June 3, the school site was set at the residence of former Hatamoto Hayato Akimoto, 5-8 Iidacho, Kojimachi-ku, Tokyo, and on August 21, an "Application for the Establishment of an Imperial Institute for the Study of the Imperial Law" was sent in the name of Vice President of the Shinto School Hei Iwashitara [[Yamada Akiyoshi]], the Vice President of Shintoism, and was approved on the 23rd of the same month. The date of registration of the [[Foundation (nonprofit)]] was later changed to the date of its establishment.國學院大學（『百二十周年小史』参照） == Public and private schools == {{Multiple image | align = right | direction = horizontal | header_align = center | footer_align = left/right/center | image1 = Nihon University Place of opening.jpg | width1 = 150 | alt1 = | caption1 = Nihon University, the site of the school's founding. | image2 = Kokugakuin University Place of opening.jpg | width2 = 150 | alt2 = | caption2 = Kokugakuin University Opening Place }} The Imperial Academy established an institution for [[research]] on its premises. The director, Akiyoshi Yamada [[Minister of Justice (Japan)|Minister of Justice]], founded the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} in 1889 (Meiji 22), followed by the Kokugakuin in the following year. He subsequently fostered public and private law schools.{{Cite web |last=[[萩市観光協会]] |date= |title=初代司法大臣で日大・国学院の学祖 山田顕義誕生地 （顕義園） |url=http://www.hagishi.com/search/detail.php?d=1100163 |access-date=2016-05-12 |publisher=萩市観光協会「ぶらり萩あるき」 |page= |quote=}} Law School In 1889, the Minister of Justice, Yamada Kengi, who was the director of the Imperial Academy, established an educational institution within the Imperial Academy for the purpose of researching Japan's unique [[:en:Code of law|Code of law]] using ancient Japanese and foreign laws as a means of improving Japan's legal system. ; Kokugakuin Following the Law School, the Kokugakuin was established in 1890 to study national history, national literature, and [[Statute|national law]], and to promote [[Kokugaku|national studies]] and to train priests as an institution for teaching the concept of the nation, or national direction and Shinto.[http://www.kokugakuin.ac.jp/guide/shuisho.html 國學院設立趣意書] == Positions held == For [[Kokugakuin University]], see [[Kokugakuin University#People and organizations related to Kokugakuin]] === President === * [[Prince Arisugawa Takahito|Prince Nobuhito Arisugawa]], February 1882 - January 1886. * [[Prince Tsunehisa Takeda]], May 1908-. * [[Prince Naruhisa Kitashirakawa]] 1908-1924 * [[Prince Kuni Kuniyoshi|Kunihiko Kuniyoshi]], November 1927 - 1930 * Prince [[Prince Kan'in Kotohito|Prince Kaniinomiya]], 1930 - 1945 * [[Prince Nashimoto Morimasa|Prince Morimasa Nashimoto]] 1945-1946 === Vice President === * [[Kuga Tatemichi]], September 1882-] * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] April 1918-June 1921 * [[:en:Egi Kazuyuki|Egi Senyuki]] August 1932-. * [[Hiranuma Kiichirō]], 1945- === Director === * [[Yamada Akiyoshi]] January 1889 - 1895 * [[Sasaki Takayuki|Takayuki Sasaki]] June 1896 - March 1910 * [[Yoshikawa Akimasa]] March 1910-March 1911 * [[Nabeshima Naohiro (Saga)|Naohiro Nabeshima]] March 1911-April 1918 * [[Hijikata Hisamoto|Hisamoto Hijikata]], 1919- * [[Eitaro Komatsubara]], 1919-1920 * [[Ichiki Kitokurō|Kitokurō Ichiki]] 1920-1925 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], February 1925-August 1932 * [[Kuniyuki Tokugawa]], 1933- * [[Yukitada Sasaki]] May 1936-March 1946 === Secretary General === * Shigetake Sugiura May 1899- * Shinichiro Yamada 1912 - 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- === Secretary === * Noboru Takayama 1902- * Momoki Kamo 1903 * Momoki Kamo April 1903-October 1905 * Iwakichi Ishikawa 1909- * Yoshiki Kuwahara 1917 * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1917- * Tomokazu Soejima 1926 (Taisho 15)- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara 1918- * Yoshiki Iwamoto 1924- * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- === Executive Director === * Yoshiki Kuwabara * Tomokazu Soejima 1933- * Noboru Takayama 1937- * [[Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat)|Shigeru Yoshida]] === Board of directors === * Sadasuke Imaizumi Toyoji Wada 1921- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shozo Kono 1935- * Shigeru Yoshida (bureaucrat) * Shozo Kono 1935- * Naoichiro Ueki 1945- == Others == As a reorganization of the former [[Home Ministry|Ministry of the Interior]] due to the separation of teachings and studies, the Imperial Academy was decided upon by a motion made after the conclusion of the Grand Council on Shintoism by Home Minister Yamada Kenyoshi, who was appointed to the Shinto Interdisciplinary Office at the time.The Imperial Academy, which was based on the [[Shinto Office Student Dormitory]] and expanded, was established from Yamada's It was established from a motion of the [[Kensho]] In 1885 [[:en:Cabinet of Japan|Cabinet System]] was established, and in 1886 [[Itō Hirobumi]] established a government official training institute. 1889 [[Meiji Constitution|The Constitution of the Empire of Japan]] was enacted, which shifted the focus from imperial studies to government-oriented [[Higher education]] system. The priesthood training institutions were transformed into official training institutions under Ito's policy of establishing the Imperial University Ordinance. Thus, the establishment of [[:en:Benefit corporation|public interest corporation]] under Act No. 89 of [[:en:1896|1894]] came into effect, and the new [[Civil law (common law)|Civil law]] of 1898 transformed the organization into a foundation (public interest corporation), which was the modern organization at the time.In the same year, the {{ill|Japan Law School|ja|日本法律学校|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Law School|qq=}} also made the same transition. == Annotations == === Notes === {{Reflist|group="note"}} === References === {{reflist}} == Bibliography == * 『皇典講究所五十年史』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|1035528}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1932nd year * 『皇典講究所改正要領』、皇典講究所、[{{NDLDC|815303}} 国会図書館デジタル化資料]、1889th year 6月 * 『皇典講究所草創期の人々』、[[Kokugakuin University|國學院大學]]、本居豊穎、1982nd year 2月 * 『明治期國學研究雑誌集成』、國學院大學、木野主計、雄松堂出版、1996th year 11月 * {{Cite book |last=新田均・武田秀章 |title=わかりやすい神道の歴史 |publisher=神社新報社 |year=2005 |isbn=9784915265051 |editor-last=神社本庁研修所 |chapter=第六章 明治維新以後（近代）、現代 |ref={{Sfnref|Nitta|Takeda|2005}} |language=ja |trans-title=An Easy-to-Understand History of Shinto. }} * {{Cite book |last1=松本久史 |title=プレステップ神道学
